newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban authorities detain dissident journalist.
newsitem.headline: Cuban authorities detain dissident journalist.

text.p: Cuban security officials detained dissident journalist Raul Rivero early on Tuesday and searched his house, dissident sources said.

The sources said Rivero, one of the best known of Cuba's dissident journalists, was driven away from his home in central Havana in the early morning. Security officials spent several hours searching his appartment.

Rivero is head of a news agency called Cuba Press, one of a handful of small and illegal news organisations set up over the last two years by dissident journalists seeking to provide an alternative to the state-controlled media in the one-party communist state.
Journalists such as Rivero cannot publish in Cuba but send their work to the United States and other countries.

Since the dissident journalist groups began emerging, several independent journalists have gone into exile. Others have been detained for short periods or questioned by security officials. Rivero was held for several hours two weeks ago.

The Paris-based journalists' rights group Reporters Sans Frontieres (Reporters Without Borders) and the New York-based Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) sent letters to President Fidel Castro on Tuesday calling for his release.

Rivero's detention follows that of four leading dissidents in mid-July. The four -- Vladimiro Roca, Martha Beatriz Roque, Felix Bonne and Rene Gomez Manzano -- have not yet been charged but authorities have said they are being investigated on suspicion of "counter-revolutionary" activities.
